name: the ❓ button's modifier test is inverted
why: Plain click and Shift-click both still 'work' with the test backwards — you simply always land on the other destination. Nothing throws, nothing looks broken, and the only symptom is that the button does the opposite of what its tooltip says.
grep: a plain click opens the GitHub help page

name: the new tab is opened without noopener
why: window.open's third argument is what stops the opened page getting a window.opener handle back into a MusicBrainz tab this script is driving. Dropping it changes nothing the user can see.
grep: a plain click opens the GitHub help page

name: the help fetch still points at the retired .txt
why: The rename is two constants that have to move together. Leaving REMOTE_HELP_URL on the .txt makes the ❓ button open the new document on GitHub while the dialog serves the old one — two different help texts from one button, with no error anywhere.

name: the dialog drops the source into a <pre> again, as it used to
why: The old behaviour, which was right for a hand-laid-out .txt and became wrong the moment the source was Markdown: every heading, table and link renders as its own syntax.
grep: headings, emphasis, code spans and links become elements

name: underscore emphasis is 'restored'
why: The plausible improvement, and the reason there is a test for the ABSENCE of a feature. CommonMark refuses intra-word underscore emphasis precisely because of identifiers like sa_enable_caa_pics; adding the rule back renders that as 'sa' + italic 'enable_caa' + 'pics' throughout a document whose nouns are mostly settings keys.
grep: a snake_case identifier is NOT italicised

name: any scheme is accepted as a link href
why: The bytes are fetched over the network at runtime. 'It is our own file' is a fact about the repository, not about what a fetch returns, and a help dialog is not where you want to find out.
grep: a non-http link renders as inert text

name: inline syntax is applied inside a fenced code block
why: A fence's whole point is that its contents are content. Rendering inline markup inside one silently eats asterisks and backticks out of the very examples the document is showing.
grep: fenced code keeps its content verbatim

name: the table separator row is not required
why: Without it, any line starting with a pipe begins a table — and a table's own separator row then becomes its first data row. The guard is what keeps the table rule from firing on prose.
grep: a pipe-led line with no separator

name: a wrapped bullet ends its list (no lazy continuation)
why: The defect this renderer actually shipped with for an afternoon. A continuation line ends the list, becomes a stray paragraph, and the next bullet opens a fresh one-item list — every fragment individually well-formed, which is why the first version of the spec could not see it and a structural probe could. The whole 'Supported pages' section rendered as six one-item lists.
grep: a wrapped bullet stays ONE item

name: a lazy continuation need not be indented
why: The indent requirement is what keeps the continuation rule from swallowing the next block: a heading, fence, table row or rule starts at column 0, so none of them can be read as continuation text. Dropping it lets a list eat the section that follows it.
grep: a heading directly under a list

name: <details> renders closed, as written
why: The obvious reading of the source, and wrong for this surface: collapsed content is still in the DOM, so the dialog's quick filter highlights matches the reader cannot see. A filter that reports hits into a closed box is worse than no filter — and searching the whole text is the only reason to be in this dialog rather than on GitHub.

edits.find: d.open = true;                          // see this function's JSDoc

grep: renders OPEN, so the quick filter

name: an in-document anchor is handed to the browser
why: The dialog is a fixed overlay with its own scroll area, so following the fragment scrolls MusicBrainz's page underneath while the table of contents appears to do nothing.
grep: an in-document anchor link scrolls the dialog

name: heading ids lose their prefix, matching GitHub's bare slug
why: Recorded as FAIL because the spec pins the prefixed href — but the interesting half is why the prefix exists at all, and no fixture can show that: it stops a heading id such as 'content' or 'header' colliding with one MusicBrainz's own page already uses. The collision needs a real page whose ids happen to match a heading in the help file, which no committed fixture has.
grep: an in-document anchor link scrolls the dialog

name: the Markdown stylesheet is injected with inline styles instead
why: Recorded as pass, honestly. MusicBrainz serves /account/* with style-src 'self' and no unsafe-inline, so a style= attribute is silently dropped THERE and works everywhere else — the whole reason this renderer uses classes and GM_addStyle. Reproducing it needs a capture of /account/applications under its real CSP, which no fixture provides: a fixture is served from the test harness and carries no CSP at all.
grep: headings, emphasis, code spans and links become elements

name: the help cache key is left on its old name
why: Recorded as pass, honestly. fetchCachedText() keys on the cache key alone and stores no URL beside the bytes, so an upgrading user with the plain-text help cached would have it fed to the Markdown renderer for up to a TTL. Every fixture starts with empty GM storage, so no test here can hold a stale value from a previous format.
